speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: asked the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health in view of the Nipah virus (NiV) high case fatality rate (CFR), whether the Ministry will (i) require health declarations and conduct screening of passengers arriving from or who have recently been in high-risk areas at our ports of entry and (ii) provide healthcare advisories and information to doctors and the public.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I seek two clarifications from the Senior Minister of State on border health measures that have been stepped up in view of the disease outbreaks overseas.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: First, will these include updating the SG Arrival Card declarations required of arriving passengers in terms of prior travel destinations?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I ask this because I checked the SG Arrival Card, and only Africa and Latin America are listed.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: My second clarification is whether this information will be shared with the health authorities for further monitoring.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, it is to make sure that there are no excessive compliance needs on the individual submitting the information card to make it seamless.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: At the same time, we do not want to end up having over-declaration for those with no symptoms.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: Whether information will be shared with the health authorities.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: I have filed similar questions and I will repeat them here.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: And what grants or subsidies are there for local firms to ensure that such research remains viable even though there is no commercial market.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: My Giam, I think Senior Minister of State Dr Koh was only answering Question No 1.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: So, anyway, we will move to Question No 2.
